'''Oliver Keith Baker''' (born July 18, 1959) is an [[American people|American]] [[experimental physics|experimental]] [[particle physics|particle physicist]] and [[astrophysicist]], the D. Allan Bromley Professor of Physics at [[Yale University]].<ref name="Bromley">{{cite web |title=Keith Baker appointed the D. Allan Bromley Professor of Physics |date=April 13, 2021 |website=Physics Department, Yale University |url=https://physics.yale.edu/news/keith-baker-appointed-d-allan-bromley-professor-physics}}</ref> He is best known for his contributions to the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]] as a member of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS Collaboration]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]], his work on [[dark matter]] and dark sector physics, and pioneering research connecting [[quantum information science]] to high-energy particle physics. In 2002, he won the Edward Alexander Bouchet Award of the [[American Physical Society]]: "For his contribution to nuclear and particle physics; for building the infrastructure to do these measurements; and for being active in outreach activities, both locally and nationally."<ref name=Bouchet2002>{{Cite web | url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Baker&first_nm=Oliver&year=2002 | title=2002 Edward A. Bouchet Award Recipient |website=American Physical Society|language=en |access-date=October 20, 2020}}</ref> In 2006, he became the first tenured [[African Americans|African American]] faculty member in the Yale physics department.<ref name="YDN2006">{{Cite web|date=September 6, 2006|title=Physics Expands by Five Profs|url=https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2006/09/06/physics-expands-by-five-profs/|access-date=October 20, 2020|website=Yale Daily News|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Oliver Keith Baker was born in [[McGehee]], [[Arkansas]] in 1959 to parents Oliver and Yvonne Baker, and grew up in [[Memphis, Tennessee]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web | url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2016/nov/07/physicist-credits-his-tillar-roots-2016/ |title = Physicist credits his Tillar roots |date=November 7, 2016 |website= Arkansas Democrat Gazette |language=en|access-date=October 20, 2020}}</ref>

Keith Baker received his B.S. in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)]] in 1981. Baker completed both his M.S. in physics and mathematics in 1984 and his Ph.D. in physics in 1987 from [[Stanford University|Stanford]] working on experimental nuclear physics.<ref name="Bouchet2002" />

== Career ==

Baker completed a post-doc at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] from 1986 to 1988 conducting research on [[Muon-catalyzed fusion|muon catalyzed fusion]], where he made the first measurement of the muon sticking probability in that process.<ref name=":0" /> After his post-doc, Baker joined [[Hampton University]] in 1989<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Oliver Keith Baker - Physicist of the African Diaspora|url=https://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/physics/baker_oliverkeith.html|access-date=2021-03-14|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> as an assistant professor in the physics department with a joint appointment as a staff scientist at [[Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility]].<ref name="HistoryMakers" /> At Hampton, he also made the first accurate measurement of the elementary amplitudes in kaon electroproduction. In 2000, he was named Endowed University Professor of Physics, and in 2002 became the founding director of the Center for the Study of the Origin and Structure of Matter (CSOM), a [[National Science Foundation]] Physics Frontier Center partnering Hampton University, [[Norfolk State University]], and [[North Carolina A&T State University]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Bouchet2002" />

In 2006, Baker began professorship at [[Yale University]] where he was the first tenured [[African Americans|African American]] faculty member in the physics department.<ref name="YDN2006" /> In 2010, Baker became director of Yale's A. W. Wright Nuclear Structure Laboratory,<ref name=HistoryMakers>{{Cite web | url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/oliver-baker | title=Oliver Baker |website= The History Makers|language=en |date=March 10, 2013 |access-date=October 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://wlab.yale.edu/ | title=Wright Laboratory |website= Yale |language=en |date=2020|access-date=October 20, 2020}}</ref> which includes state-of-the-art facilities for the study of [[neutrinos]], dark matter and [[fundamental physics]]. In February 2021 he was appointed to Yale's D. Allan Bromley Professorship of Physics.<ref name="Bromley" />

== Research ==

=== ATLAS and the Higgs boson ===
Baker is a member of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS Collaboration]], which in 2012 discovered the [[Higgs boson]] predicted by the [[Standard Model]].<ref name="ATLAS_Higgs_Discovery">The ATLAS Collaboration, "Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC", [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S037026931200857X?via%3Dihub Phys. Lett. B 716:1-29 (2012)].</ref> He led the construction of components of the ATLAS [[Transition radiation detector|Transition Radiation Tracker]] (TRT) and was part of the team that carried out the [[machine learning]] analysis contributing to the discovery. He serves as the Yale ATLAS team leader and Yale ATLAS Institute representative.

=== Dark sector searches ===
Baker originated the ATLAS analysis searching for [[Hidden sector|dark sector]] phenomena through exotic decays of the Higgs boson to four leptons, setting new limits on light gauge bosons beyond the Standard Model.<ref>The ATLAS Collaboration, "Search for new light gauge bosons in Higgs boson decays to four-lepton final states in pp collisions at √s = 8 TeV with the ATLAS detector", [https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.92.092001 Phys. Rev. D 92, 092001 (2015)].</ref> He has also studied photon–paraphoton kinetic mixing as a possible explanation for the propagation of ultra-high-energy [[cosmic rays]] from [[BL Lacertae]] objects.<ref>O. K. Baker and R. J. Anantua, "TeV gamma rays from distant BL Lacs and photon-paraphoton kinetic mixing" [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S037026931000540X?via%3Dihub Phys. Lett. B 290:25-28 (2010)]</ref>

=== Quantum information science in high-energy physics ===
With [[Dmitri Kharzeev]], Baker co-pioneered the application of [[quantum information]] concepts to LHC collisions, demonstrating a connection between [[quantum entanglement]] and the apparent thermalization observed in particle production in proton–proton collisions.<ref>O. K. Baker and D. E. Kharzeev, "Thermal radiation and entanglement in proton-proton collisions at the LHC", [https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.98.054007 Phys. Rev. D 98, 054007 (2018)].</ref> He is the academic editor and co-author of the book ''Quantum Entanglement in High Energy Physics'' (IntechOpen).

=== Axion searches ===
Baker's group is involved in the search for [[axion]] dark matter at Yale's [[Wright Laboratory]]. The group is contributing detector development to the Axion Longitudinal Plasma HAloscope (ALPHA) experiment, which employs a novel plasma haloscope to search for higher-mass axions.

== Awards and honors ==
* Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (elected 2022)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.yale.edu/2022/04/28/eight-yale-faculty-members-elected-american-academy-arts-and-sciences |title=Eight Yale faculty members elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |publisher=Yale News |date=April 28, 2022}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (elected 2021), for "leadership in the construction of the ATLAS TRT tracker and its use in innovative searches for new physics and new phenomena, including the use of the Higgs as a probe of the dark sector"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.yale.edu/2021/10/13/baker-gozar-elected-fellows-american-physical-society |title=Baker, Gozar elected fellows by the American Physical Society |publisher=Yale News |date=October 13, 2021}}</ref>
* U.S. ATLAS Distinguished Researcher (2017)
* Inducted into [[Arkansas Black Hall of Fame]] (2006)<ref name=":0" />
* [[Edward Alexander Bouchet Award]] from the [[American Physical Society]] (2002)<ref name="Bouchet2002" /><ref name="HistoryMakers" />
* Elmer Imes Award for Outstanding Research from the [[National Society of Black Physicists]]<ref name="HistoryMakers" />
* E. L. Hamm, Sr. Distinguished Teaching Award<ref name="HistoryMakers" />
